properties.name: Crossing of the Bavispe
properties.reasoning: The book names no crossing point. The Bavispe runs along the eastern foot of the Sierra La Madera past Granados, Huásabas and Villa Hidalgo, so a wolf leaving the eastern slopes crosses it there. The circle is centred on that reach and reaches Granados and Villa Hidalgo (16.6 km each way).

properties.name: Between Clanton and Foster draws
properties.reasoning: The high country between Clanton Draw (GNIS 887634) and Foster Draw (GNIS 889164), which lie 3 km apart.

properties.name: Robertson's crossfence
properties.reasoning: Between the Cloverdale Creek road and the Guadalupe pass. The Robertson family ran the Cloverdale Ranch from the early 1900s (Range Magazine, winter 2000, rangemagazine.com/archives/stories/winter00/bootheel.htm), so the fence is likely theirs. GNIS has no Robertson ranch and the ranch's bounds are not known here; the circle covers the ground between the road and the pass.

properties.name: Ranch house on the volcanic plain
properties.reasoning: Past the Guadalupe pass and before the boundary. The book crosses a broad volcanic plain here. The Geronimo–San Bernardino volcanic field covers the northern San Bernardino Valley in basalt, from Cochise County into Hidalgo County and Sonora (New Mexico Geological Society guidebook; Arizona Geological Survey), which is the ground south-west of the pass. The ranch house itself is unnamed.

properties.name: The boundary, a monument in sight
properties.reasoning: Boundary monuments stand along 31°20′ N here. The circle covers the stretch south of the volcanic plain and north of the Cajon Bonita.

properties.name: The mud-house settlement
properties.reasoning: Unnamed. Between the crossing at Colonia Oaxaca and Colonia Morelos.

properties.name: The hacienda
properties.reasoning: Unnamed in the book. It lies by a river within a day of Colonia Morelos and the Pilares Teras; the circle is centred near Morelos and sized to that reach. Earlier notes placed it on the Batepito plain, but the book does not name Batepito.

properties.name: A promontory above the Bavispe
properties.reasoning: Two days later, from a promontory, he sees the Bavispe seeming to flow the wrong way and works out that he has crossed back through the mountains to where the river runs north along the eastern side of the Sierras. That north-running reach is the upper Bavispe between Bacerac and Bavispe town, so the promontory is on the sierra's eastern edge above it; the circle covers that edge.

properties.name: Among the Indians in the Sierras
properties.reasoning: He wanders the high country for weeks and Indians feed him; the book names no range or camp. The circle covers the Sierra El Tigre country south of the mining town and west of the upper Bavispe, between his stop at El Tigre and his descent to the river.

properties.name: The eastern escarpment above the Bavispe barranca
properties.reasoning: From the eastern escarpment he looks east over the Bavispe's barranca to the Carretas Plain beyond, then goes down, sleeps by the river and rides north along the river track to a ford. So the escarpment is on the sierra's eastern edge upriver (south) of Huisiachepic; the circle is set south-west of the Huisiachepic estimate.

properties.name: Huisiachepic, the heretic's town
properties.reasoning: No gazetteer or source has Huisiachepic (see docs/open-questions.md). The text puts it across a ford on the upper Bavispe, reached by riding north along the river, and several days upriver (south) of Tamichopa. The estimate is the midpoint of the river reach between Mesa Tres Ríos and Huachinera, 28.2 km straight-line south of Tamichopa.

properties.name: A pass in the Guadalupes on the old Cloverdale road
properties.reasoning: He rides the old road from Douglas to Cloverdale all day and crosses a cold pass in the Guadalupe Mountains, with old names carved in the rock, and looks down on the Animas Plain at dusk. The book does not name the pass; the circle is where a road east from Douglas toward Cloverdale crosses the range, north of the low pass of J2.

properties.name: Sanders' (the SK Bar)
properties.reasoning: Old man Sanders and Leona tell him what happened. No source names an SK Bar ranch (see docs/open-questions.md); the text puts it nine miles north of the Parham house by road, so the estimate is about 14.5 km north of Cloverdale.

properties.name: The Websters' (Boyd)
properties.reasoning: Boyd is lodging with the Websters on the east side of Lordsburg; the book gives no street. The circle covers the east side of town.

properties.name: Leaving the Websters', Lordsburg
properties.reasoning: The brothers leave the Websters' with the shotgun, money and food, and cross the Southern Pacific tracks out of Lordsburg.

properties.name: Camp on the alkali flats
properties.reasoning: They camp on alkali flats the text puts fifteen miles west of Lordsburg, burning fenceposts. Fifteen miles due west of Lordsburg (pyproj, WGS 84) falls on the playa west of town; the circle allows for the direction.

properties.name: Noon at the San Simon River
properties.reasoning: They cross a low range and descend into the San Simon Valley where it comes down from the north, and noon at the river under cottonwoods. GNIS pins the valley 54 km north of Bowie, so the stop is a point on the San Simon River between the state line and San Simon town (see the place's reasoning).

properties.name: Across the highway east of Bowie
properties.reasoning: In the evening they cross the highway a little east of Bowie and strike the old road south through the Dos Cabezas.

properties.name: The eastern rim of the escarpment at sunrise
properties.reasoning: From Bacerac a rough trail climbs through pine and scrub oak; the next morning

properties.name: The plains, with the Tarahumaras
properties.reasoning: Below the rim they cross prairie to a ciénega where Tarahumaras afoot are watering, headed back into the sierras. The circle covers the plain between the escarpment and Colonia Juárez.

properties.name: The girl, at a fire in an oak grove
properties.reasoning: Riding south on the road toward San Diego they see a fire in a grove of oaks east of the road, where two men hold the girl; Boyd stampedes their horses. The circle is east of the road between Casas Grandes and San Diego (15.8 km apart).

properties.name: The opera company stranded on the Madera road
properties.reasoning: Late in the day they find the troupe's caravan in a field beside the road a few miles south of Las Varas on the Madera road, with a dead mule on the road nearby. The circle is centred 5 km (about three miles) from Las Varas toward Madera, on the bearing between the two towns (200 degrees, pyproj, WGS 84).

properties.name: Camps by the river
properties.reasoning: They camp in an oak grove by a river, then leave the dirt road for a path past a pepper field and an irrigation ditch to a ford where boys are swimming. The book names neither the river nor a town; the circle covers the country along the road between the opera camp and Madera.

properties.name: Crossing of the old wagon road to Namiquipa
properties.reasoning: After three days' riding they reach the crossing of the old wagon road that runs from La Norteña in the western sierras across the Babícora plains and the Santa María valley to Namiquipa. Next morning the girl rides away east toward Namiquipa, which is 57 km due east of the circle's centre (bearing 92 degrees). The book's compass does not close here: the brothers then ride south into pinewoods and reach Las Varas, which lies to the north, two days later. The circle is wide for that reason.

properties.name: The steer herd on the road to Boquilla
properties.reasoning: In the evening, on the road east to Boquilla, they meet about a thousand steers being trailed from La Quemada to the pens at Naco; after dark they pass a hamlet of log houses on the high plain. The circle is on the road between Las Varas and the Babícora lake.

properties.name: Their horses, up from the lake
properties.reasoning: Next morning two young vaqueros drive their own horses up from a high-country laguna south of the road, and the brothers rope Niño and Bailey. The laguna is the Babícora lake (GeoNames 4017246, 29.35 N, 107.83 W); the circle is on the road north of it.

properties.name: The manco's riders, the Boquilla hacienda in sight
properties.reasoning: At noon, with the walls of the hacienda in the distance and the lake to the south, riders led by a one-armed man block the road and take the horses. The circle is on the road west of La Boquilla, east of the lake.

properties.name: Following the horses' tracks north
properties.reasoning: They ride back west for an hour to where the tracks leave the road above the lake and follow them north all afternoon, sighting the riders at twilight, and camp in a swale. The circle is north of the lake.

properties.name: Quijada's remuda
properties.reasoning: Next day they reach an east-west road, follow it east to a crossroads where a track comes down from the mountains to the north, and Quijada, superintendent of the Nahuerichic division, leads them up the road to the remuda and lets Boyd cut out three horses. The book gives no distances; the circle is north-east of the tracking camp.

properties.name: Off the road north of Boquilla, west to a river
properties.reasoning: They leave the road a mile north of the town and go west to a river with nine horses, turning the Boquilla horses back. The book does not name the river; the circle is north-west of La Boquilla.

properties.name: The dry camp after the night ride
properties.reasoning: They cross the river upcountry, ride all night through open country away from it, and make a dry camp toward morning in a burned grove on a rise a mile west of the river. The circle is between Boquilla and San José, which are 48 km apart (bearing 340 degrees).

properties.name: The river camp where Boyd is shot
properties.reasoning: They camp in a cottonwood grove by the river near San José. At dawn five riders come upriver on the far bank and Boyd is shot from across the river. The book gives no distance from the pueblito; the circle is around it.

properties.name: The road where the workers' truck takes Boyd
properties.reasoning: Billy rides double with Boyd into open country, sees a vehicle crossing in the distance, and on the dirt road meets a flatbed truck of farmworkers coming from the south; they lift Boyd aboard and it goes on north. The circle is between the river camp and the main road north to Mata Ortiz.

properties.name: The blind man's house
properties.reasoning: Alone, Billy leads his horse up an arroyo, sees a light far to the north at dusk and goes toward it; near midnight he reaches a fence, turns east to a gate and rides up a clay track to a lone house, where the blind man and his wife take him in. The circle is north of the shooting, about a day and a half south of Mata Ortiz by the text's timing.

properties.name: The desert crossroads on the main road north
properties.reasoning: Next morning he rides north along the road and before noon strikes the main road north to Casas Grandes at an empty desert crossroads; he sleeps in a field near the river breaks and rides on in rain. The circle is on the road south of Mata Ortiz.

properties.name: Within earshot of the Las Varas crossing
properties.reasoning: He rides all day, meets the workers' truck in the evening, and in the night hears a train whistle for the crossing at Las Varas. The circle is north-east of Las Varas, on the way to Boquilla.

properties.name: A stream of the Santa María headwaters
properties.reasoning: An hour along the road west he sleeps beside a stream, one of the Santa María's headwaters, and in the morning the girl rides past on his mother's old horse. The circle is centred 4 km west of Santa Ana. The real Namiquipa lies north-north-east, not west (see docs/open-questions.md).

properties.name: Camp at the edge of the lake
properties.reasoning: They ride on west into the dark and camp at the edge of the lake. The circle is on the north-west shore of the Babícora lake (GeoNames 4017246), on the way to Las Varas.

properties.name: Camp on the river south of Mata Ortiz
properties.reasoning: They take the road north by the railroad; the ride to San Diego takes three days, and the last night they camp on a gravel bar on the river some miles south of Mata Ortiz while cranes fly south. The circle is about 9 km south of Mata Ortiz on the river.

properties.name: Álamo
properties.reasoning: He passes back north through the mesa hamlets of Álamo and Galeana, places he had come through before. Which Álamo is unresolved (docs/open-questions.md): the circle is centred on the best estimate, GeoNames 4018952, 15 km south-west of San Buenaventura, and covers El Álamo north-east of the town too.

properties.name: Boyd lifted onto the workers' truck
properties.reasoning: Billy sees the farmworkers lift Boyd onto their truck, which goes on north (3-08); from here Boyd's road is known only from what others tell Billy. The circle is the same as J4's.

properties.name: The shallow salt lake
properties.reasoning: At sunset he reaches a shallow salt lake his horse will not cross, rides south along the flats with snow on Gillespie Mountain and the Animas Peaks beyond, and camps by an old fence. The lake is Playas Lake (GNIS 893357, 31.88 N, 108.59 W), the salt flat west of the Little Hatchets; the circle is its southern end.

properties.name: The old Playas road over the mountains
properties.reasoning: In the morning they cross the lake, strike the old Playas road before noon and follow it west into the mountains, with snow in the pass. The book does not name the pass; the circle is in the Animas Mountains west of the lake.

properties.name: Sanders' (the SK Bar)
properties.reasoning: He reaches the Sanders ranch two hours after dark, eats supper and will not stay the night. In 4-02 it is called the SK Bar. No source names the ranch (docs/open-questions.md); the circle is the same estimate as J3's, nine miles north of the Parham house.

properties.name: Camp on the Animas Plain
properties.reasoning: He camps that night on the broad Animas Plain and sees lightning far to the south beyond the Hatchet Mountains. The circle is on the open plain south-east of the Sanders estimate.

properties.name: The SK Bar gate
properties.reasoning: Two days later he reaches the SK Bar gate, learns that Miller died on Kwajalein, and stays the night in the rain. The circle is the J3 estimate (docs/open-questions.md).

properties.name: Camp on the plain by the lake, the red plane
properties.reasoning: On the road east toward La Boquilla a north wind blows dust off Babícora beyond the lake, a red plane flies in from the west, and he camps on the plain. The circle is north-east of the Babícora lake.

properties.name: The high country of the Babícora
properties.reasoning: For days he camps in the swales of the Babícora high country and watches vaqueros working whiteface cattle on mules. The circle covers the plains around the lake and the ranch headquarters.

properties.name: Quijada's cabin
properties.reasoning: One evening he follows a road west toward a gap in the mountains and after dark reaches a lone weatherboard cabin on the plain, where Quijada, still manager of the Nahuerichic division, tells him where Boyd fell and lies. Next day he rides north all day to San Buenaventura, so the circle is about a day's ride (47 km) south-south-west of it. It is 57 km from Nahuerachi, the open-questions pick for the division's name.

properties.name: Boyd's grave, on the Gallego road
properties.reasoning: The cemetery is on a bench in the low hills east of town, a mile or so up the old road to Gallego, with the Sierra del Nido in sight. He finds the board cross by the south wall and digs all day. The circle is centred 1.6 km due east of the town point.

properties.name: Past the lights of Casas Grandes, to the west
properties.reasoning: Near midnight he leaves with the bones on the packhorse, crosses the highway and heads across country with the polestar to his right. In two nights' riding he passes the lights of Casas Grandes off to the west, so he is east of the town; the circle is 15 km east of it.

properties.name: The Casas Grandes River, across the Guzmán road
properties.reasoning: He crosses the old road coming down from Guzmán and Sabinal, strikes the Casas Grandes River and takes the trail north along its bank. The circle is on the river south of Corralitos.

properties.name: The attack on the river trail, and the gypsies' camp
properties.reasoning: An hour north of the town four riders stop him on the trail, cut open the bones and stab Niño; the next day gypsies hauling an old airplane north camp with him by the river and doctor the horse (4-06, 4-07). An hour's ride is about 6 km; the circle is centred 5.8 km north of Corralitos.

properties.name: The border, west of Dog Springs
properties.reasoning: Four days later he sets out north along the river with the bones on a travois; it takes three days to reach the border, where he passes the first boundary obelisk west of Dog Springs and an old dry reservoir. No Dog Springs is known on the line (docs/open-questions.md); the circle is the best estimate, the boundary south of Hermanas.

properties.name: The little cemetery south of Animas
properties.reasoning: He buys a spade and goes south from the town to a little cemetery, where he buries Boyd; the sheriff tells him to report at Lordsburg. GNIS lists no cemetery here; the circle is just south of the town.

properties.name: Over the Black Range
properties.reasoning: He crosses the Black Range on the old road east. The book names no pass; the road from San Lorenzo crosses the range at Emory Pass (GNIS 906157), where the circle is centred.

properties.name: The ruined waystation by the blacktop
properties.reasoning: Beyond the range he crosses a plain of catclaw and creosote, strikes the blacktop a few miles on, sees the Organ Mountains about eighty miles off, and turns back along the highway to three ruined adobes with a rusted gas pump, once a waystation. There he drives off the crippled dog, and wakes to the false dawn (4-09). The circle is on the plain east of Hillsboro; its centre is 112 km (70 miles) straight-line from the Organ Mountains point (GNIS 920657, pyproj, WGS 84), and Emory Pass is 131 km (81 miles), so the book's eighty miles fits the range's eastern foot.
